findings.claim: In bullet both sides give away about 0.9 expected points per game and the opponents give away a few thousandths more than the player.
findings.metric: sum of ep_loss over a side's moves, mean per game; difference = opponents minus player (positive = opponents gave away more)
findings.caveat: ep_loss is relative to engine-best play and clipped at zero; the difference is paired within games. higher_is_better refers to the difference (opponents minus player).

findings.claim: In blitz the player and the opponents give away the same expected points per game.
findings.metric: sum of ep_loss over a side's moves, mean per game; difference = opponents minus player (positive = opponents gave away more)
findings.caveat: ep_loss is relative to engine-best play and clipped at zero; the difference is paired within games.

findings.claim: In rapid the opponents give away about 0.025 expected points per game more than the player.
findings.metric: sum of ep_loss over a side's moves, mean per game; difference = opponents minus player (positive = opponents gave away more)
findings.caveat: Rapid has only 588 games.

findings.claim: In bullet the player loses more centipawns per game than the opponents, although not more expected points.
findings.metric: sum of cp_loss over a side's moves, mean per game
findings.caveat: cp_loss is the secondary measure; big centipawn swings in already decided positions cost few expected points.

findings.claim: The player's bullet score is within a hundredth of the model's expectation at move 1.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus model expected points at move 1 (pre-game ratings and time control)

findings.claim: The player's blitz score exceeds the model's move-1 expectation by about two hundredths, with the CI touching zero.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus model expected points at move 1 (pre-game ratings and time control)

findings.claim: The player's rapid score exceeds the model's move-1 expectation by about four hundredths of a point per game.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus model expected points at move 1 (pre-game ratings and time control)
findings.caveat: Rapid has only 588 games.

findings.claim: In blitz the part of the score the engine-based decomposition cannot see (resignations, flags, end-of-game model error, ep_loss clipping) is positive for the player.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus (ep at move 1 minus player's ep lost plus opponents' ep lost)
findings.caveat: Where positive, the residual reflects games that ended before the board said so plus the clipping of ep_loss at zero. Bullet residual is -0.000 [-0.012, 0.011], rapid 0.018 [-0.004, 0.042].

findings.claim: In bullet the player's score exceeds the model's expectation after the last move by a hundredth of a point per game.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus model expected points after the last move
findings.caveat: Blitz is also 0.010 [0.001, 0.018]; rapid -0.005 [-0.019, 0.009]. Reflects the end-of-game model error and games ended by flag or resignation.

findings.claim: In bullet openings the player loses slightly more expected points per move than the opponents.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss per move, opening phase (material heuristic); difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: 'Opening' is the material heuristic and includes many moves beyond book.

findings.claim: In bullet middlegames the player loses marginally fewer expected points per move than the opponents, with the CI touching zero.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss per move, middlegame phase; difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: In cp terms the player loses more than opponents in bullet middlegames (4.8 [2.9, 6.7] cp per move); those are big swings in already decided positions.

findings.claim: Bullet endgames are the player's cleanest phase relative to the field: fewer expected points lost per move than the opponents.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss per move, endgame phase; difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: The one cell cleaner than the opponents' on every measure (mean ep_loss, share >= 0.1, share >= 0.2).

findings.claim: In blitz openings the player and the opponents lose the same expected points per move.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss per move, opening phase; difference = player minus opponents

findings.claim: In blitz middlegames the player loses slightly more expected points per move than the opponents, CI including zero.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss per move, middlegame phase; difference = player minus opponents

findings.claim: In blitz endgames the player and the opponents lose the same expected points per move.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss per move, endgame phase; difference = player minus opponents

findings.claim: In rapid openings the player and the opponents lose the same expected points per move.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss per move, opening phase; difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Rapid has only 588 games.

findings.claim: In rapid middlegames the player and the opponents lose the same expected points per move.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss per move, middlegame phase; difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Rapid has only 588 games.

findings.claim: In rapid endgames the player loses fewer expected points per move than the opponents.
findings.metric: mean ep_loss per move, endgame phase; difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Rapid has only 588 games (284 reaching an endgame).

findings.section: Share of moves losing ≥ 0.1 expected points
findings.claim: In bullet endgames the player makes fewer moves losing at least 0.1 expected points than the opponents.
findings.metric: share of moves with ep_loss >= 0.1, endgame phase; difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: All other phase/time-class cells for the >= 0.1 share have CIs including zero.

findings.claim: In bullet endgames the player makes fewer moves losing at least 0.2 expected points than the opponents.
findings.metric: share of moves with ep_loss >= 0.2, endgame phase; difference = player minus opponents

findings.claim: In blitz openings the player makes slightly fewer moves losing at least 0.2 expected points than the opponents, CI touching zero.
findings.metric: share of moves with ep_loss >= 0.2, opening phase; difference = player minus opponents

findings.claim: Blitz middlegame moves losing at least 0.2 expected points are the cell where the player's big errors are most frequent relative to the opponents, with the CI touching zero.
findings.metric: share of moves with ep_loss >= 0.2, middlegame phase; difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: CI touches zero; the >= 0.3 share in the same cell is 0.0151 vs 0.0135, difference 0.0016 [-0.0003, 0.0035].

findings.claim: In blitz middlegames the player's tail of moves losing at least 0.3 expected points is slightly fatter than the opponents', CI including zero.
findings.metric: share of moves with ep_loss >= 0.3, middlegame phase; difference = player minus opponents

findings.claim: In rapid endgames the player makes fewer moves losing at least 0.3 expected points than the opponents.
findings.metric: share of moves with ep_loss >= 0.3, endgame phase; difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Rapid has only 588 games (284 reaching an endgame).

findings.claim: In bullet middlegames the player loses more centipawns per move than the opponents, but not more expected points.
findings.metric: mean cp_loss per move (evals clipped to +/-1000), middlegame phase; difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Secondary measure; those are big swings in positions already decided (the ep_loss difference in the same cell is -0.0006 [-0.0012, -0.0000]).

findings.claim: In blitz openings the player loses fewer centipawns per move than the opponents.
findings.metric: mean cp_loss per move, opening phase; difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Secondary measure.

findings.claim: In rapid openings the player loses fewer centipawns per move than the opponents.
findings.metric: mean cp_loss per move, opening phase; difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Secondary measure; rapid has only 588 games.

findings.claim: In rapid endgames the player loses fewer centipawns per move than the opponents.
findings.metric: mean cp_loss per move, endgame phase; difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Secondary measure; rapid has only 588 games.

findings.claim: In bullet middlegames the player blunders (cp_loss >= 300) more often per move than the opponents.
findings.metric: share of moves with cp_loss >= 300, middlegame phase; difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Secondary measure; the ep-based shares in the same cell do not differ (>= 0.1: -0.003 [-0.007, 0.000]).

findings.claim: In blitz openings the player blunders (cp_loss >= 300) less often per move than the opponents.
findings.metric: share of moves with cp_loss >= 300, opening phase; difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Secondary measure.

findings.claim: In bullet about half of all expected points the player gives away come from the 9% of moves that lose at least 0.1.
findings.metric: share of a side's total ep lost that came from moves with ep_loss >= 0.1 (the share of such moves is 0.091 for the player, 0.092 for opponents)
findings.caveat: Descriptive ratio over the whole class, no CI.

findings.claim: In blitz more than half of all expected points the player gives away come from the 10% of moves that lose at least 0.1.
findings.metric: share of a side's total ep lost that came from moves with ep_loss >= 0.1 (the share of such moves is 0.101 for the player, 0.103 for opponents)
findings.caveat: Descriptive ratio over the whole class, no CI.

findings.claim: In rapid more than half of all expected points the player gives away come from the 10% of moves that lose at least 0.1.
findings.metric: share of a side's total ep lost that came from moves with ep_loss >= 0.1 (the share of such moves is 0.096 for the player, 0.097 for opponents)
findings.caveat: Descriptive ratio over the whole class, no CI.

findings.claim: In bullet, the loser signs the defeat with an identifiable own move costing at least 0.05 expected points in 54% of the player's losses and 58% of the player's wins.
findings.metric: share of decided games with a loser's own decisive blunder (costliest move of the final slide from the last playable position, P(win) >= 20%, lost on the board < 10%, ep_loss >= 0.05); player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins
findings.caveat: By construction the decisive move is always the loser's; the complement is games lost without a 0.05 move or lost while still alive. Strict thresholds (>= 30% / < 15%) give 0.676 [0.653, 0.698] vs 0.693 [0.672, 0.714].

findings.claim: In blitz, the loser signs the defeat with an identifiable own move in 52% of the player's losses and 53% of the player's wins.
findings.metric: share of decided games with a loser's own decisive blunder (ep_loss >= 0.05 in the final slide); player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins

findings.claim: In rapid, the player's losses have an identifiable own decisive blunder far less often (47%) than the opponents' losses do (68%), the rest being lost while still alive.
findings.metric: share of decided games with a loser's own decisive blunder (ep_loss >= 0.05 in the final slide); player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins
findings.caveat: Rapid has only 588 games. Strict thresholds give 0.644 [0.581, 0.704] vs 0.809 [0.763, 0.852].

findings.claim: About one bullet loss in ten is lost on the board without any single move of the loser costing 0.05 expected points, for both sides.
findings.metric: share of decided games lost on the board (loser's P(win) < 10%) where no move of the loser's final slide cost >= 0.05; player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins

findings.claim: In bullet 37% of the player's losses ended while the model still gave the player at least a 10% win chance after the last own move, against 32% of the opponents' losses.
findings.metric: share of decided games in which the loser's P(win) after their last own move was still >= 10% (ended by flag, resignation, abandonment or a mate the model still gave chances against); player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins
findings.caveat: The bullet model keeps a real flag chance alive even at +10, so almost half the mated losers count as still alive; the player also out-performs the pooled model in every bin, so the model-relative level is not absolute. Q4 and Q7 take this up.

findings.claim: In blitz 42% of the player's losses ended while the model still gave the player at least a 10% win chance, against 39% of the opponents' losses.
findings.metric: share of decided games in which the loser's P(win) after their last own move was still >= 10%; player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins
findings.caveat: Judged by a model that is under-confident at the extremes and that the player out-performs in every bin.

findings.claim: In rapid 48% of the player's losses ended while the model still gave the player at least a 10% win chance, against 26% of the opponents' losses.
findings.metric: share of decided games in which the loser's P(win) after their last own move was still >= 10%; player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins
findings.caveat: Rapid has only 588 games; 66% of the player's rapid losses are resignations and 62% of those were still alive by the model.

findings.section: Games lost while still alive, by how they ended
findings.claim: Among the player's bullet losses by resignation, 65% were resigned while the model still gave at least a 10% win chance, against 60% of the opponents' resignations.
findings.metric: share of losses by resignation where the loser's P(win) after their last own move was still >= 10%; player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins
findings.caveat: Resignations are only 14% of the player's bullet losses; the model is under-confident at the extremes.

findings.section: Games lost while still alive, by how they ended
findings.claim: Among the player's blitz losses by resignation, 57% were resigned while the model still gave at least a 10% win chance, against 44% of the opponents' resignations.
findings.metric: share of losses by resignation where the loser's P(win) after their last own move was still >= 10%; player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins
findings.caveat: The model is under-confident at the extremes; 'alive' is model-relative.

findings.section: Games lost while still alive, by how they ended
findings.claim: Among the player's rapid losses by resignation, 62% were resigned while the model still gave at least a 10% win chance, against 33% of the opponents' resignations.
findings.metric: share of losses by resignation where the loser's P(win) after their last own move was still >= 10%; player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins
findings.caveat: Rapid has only 588 games; the model is under-confident at the extremes.

findings.section: Games lost while still alive, by how they ended
findings.claim: Timeouts are 48% of the player's bullet losses and 62% of the opponents' bullet losses.
findings.metric: share of decided games ended by the loser's timeout; player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins
findings.caveat: Descriptive share, no CI. Of those timeouts, 0.19 [0.17, 0.22] of the player's and 0.21 [0.19, 0.24] of the opponents' were still alive by the model.

findings.section: Games lost while still alive, by how they ended
findings.claim: In bullet almost half of the player's losses by checkmate were still 'alive' by the model after the last own move, because the clock term keeps a flag chance open.
findings.metric: share of losses by checkmate where the loser's P(win) after their last own move was still >= 10%; player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins
findings.caveat: A model artefact: the bullet clock term keeps a real flag chance alive for the side about to be mated, even at -10 with the opponent short of time.

findings.section: Games lost while still alive, by how they ended
findings.claim: When the player's bullet loss ended while still alive, the model's P(win) after the last own move averaged about a quarter.
findings.metric: loser's P(win) after last own move, mean over games lost while still alive (>= 10%); player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins

findings.section: What the decisive blunders look like
findings.claim: The player's decisive bullet blunder costs about 0.18 expected points, the same as the opponents'.
findings.metric: ep_loss of the loser's decisive move, mean over games with a decisive blunder; player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins
findings.caveat: Loser's P(win) around the move: 0.22 [0.21, 0.23] before, 0.10 [0.10, 0.11] after.

findings.section: What the decisive blunders look like
findings.claim: The player's decisive blitz blunder costs about 0.23 expected points, the same as the opponents'.
findings.metric: ep_loss of the loser's decisive move, mean over games with a decisive blunder; player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins

findings.section: What the decisive blunders look like
findings.claim: The player's decisive rapid blunder costs about 0.27 expected points, the opponents' about 0.24.
findings.metric: ep_loss of the loser's decisive move, mean over games with a decisive blunder; player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins
findings.caveat: Rapid has only 588 games.

findings.section: What the decisive blunders look like
findings.claim: In bullet the decisive blunder is mostly an endgame move, for the player and the opponents alike.
findings.metric: share of decisive blunders made in the endgame phase (material heuristic); player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins
findings.caveat: Opening 0.11 [0.09, 0.13], middlegame 0.34 [0.31, 0.38] for the player; phase is the material heuristic.

findings.section: What the decisive blunders look like
findings.claim: In blitz the decisive blunder is mostly an endgame move, for the player and the opponents alike.
findings.metric: share of decisive blunders made in the endgame phase (material heuristic); player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins
findings.caveat: Opening 0.13 [0.10, 0.16], middlegame 0.34 [0.30, 0.38] for the player.

findings.section: What the decisive blunders look like
findings.claim: In rapid the decisive blunder is more often a middlegame move than in bullet or blitz; the phase profile is the same for both sides.
findings.metric: share of decisive blunders made in the endgame phase (material heuristic); player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins
findings.caveat: Middlegame 0.41 [0.32, 0.51] for the player, 0.43 [0.36, 0.50] for the opponents; rapid has only 588 games.

findings.section: What the decisive blunders look like
findings.claim: The decisive bullet blunder comes some 18 plies before the end of the game.
findings.metric: plies from the loser's decisive move to the end of the game, mean; player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins

findings.section: What the decisive blunders look like
findings.claim: In bullet the decisive blunder is the very move played from the last playable position in a bit over half of the cases.
findings.metric: share of decisive blunders that are the move played from the last playable position (P(win) >= 20%); player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins

findings.section: What the decisive blunders look like
findings.claim: The player's decisive bullet blunder is made with about 23 seconds on the clock, the opponents' with about 22.
findings.metric: mover's clock before the decisive move, mean; player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins

findings.section: What the decisive blunders look like
findings.claim: The player's decisive blitz blunder is made with about 99 seconds on the clock, the opponents' with about 112.
findings.metric: mover's clock before the decisive move, mean; player = player's losses, opponents = player's wins

findings.section: 4. Converting winning positions and swindling lost ones
findings.claim: From positions the model rated at least 80% for the side to win, the player converts bullet games more often than the opponents do.
findings.metric: P(win | own P(win) reached >= 80% at some point); opponents' rate is the same quantity from their side in the same games; difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: The pooled model is under-confident at the extremes and the player out-performs it in every bin: absolute rates are model-relative, the you-vs-them gap is the robust part.

findings.section: 4. Converting winning positions and swindling lost ones
findings.claim: From positions rated at least 80%, the player converts blitz games more often than the opponents do.
findings.metric: P(win | own P(win) reached >= 80% at some point); difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Absolute rates are model-relative; the you-vs-them gap is the robust part.

findings.section: 4. Converting winning positions and swindling lost ones
findings.claim: From positions rated at least 80%, the player converts rapid games about 11 points more often than the opponents do.
findings.metric: P(win | own P(win) reached >= 80% at some point); difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Rapid has only 588 games; absolute rates are model-relative.

findings.section: 4. Converting winning positions and swindling lost ones
findings.claim: In rapid the player reaches a position rated at least 80% in half the games, more often than the opponents do.
findings.metric: share of games in which a side's P(win) reached >= 80% at some point

findings.section: 4. Converting winning positions and swindling lost ones
findings.claim: After falling to a position rated 20% or less, the player avoids losing bullet games more often than the opponents do.
findings.metric: P(did not lose | own P(win) fell to <= 20% at some point); difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Largely by winning on time: 0.69 [0.62, 0.74] of the player's bullet swindle wins came by the opponent flagging, against 0.58 [0.51, 0.64] of theirs.

findings.section: 4. Converting winning positions and swindling lost ones
findings.claim: After falling to a position rated 20% or less, the player avoids losing blitz games more often than the opponents do.
findings.metric: P(did not lose | own P(win) fell to <= 20% at some point); difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Absolute rates are model-relative; the you-vs-them gap is the robust part.

findings.section: 4. Converting winning positions and swindling lost ones
findings.claim: After falling to a position rated 20% or less, the player avoids losing rapid games about 10 points more often than the opponents do.
findings.metric: P(did not lose | own P(win) fell to <= 20% at some point); difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Rapid has only 588 games; absolute rates are model-relative.

findings.claim: Most of the player's bullet swindle wins came by the opponent flagging, a larger share than for the opponents' swindle wins.
findings.metric: share of swindle wins (fell to <= 20%, then won) in which the other side lost on time
findings.n: n=284 player swindle wins, n=198 opponents
findings.caveat: As a share of all swindles: 0.48 (player) vs 0.37 (opponents); 0.19 vs 0.23 of swindles were draws by timeout vs insufficient material.

findings.claim: In blitz about a fifth of each side's swindle wins came by the other side flagging, the same for the player and the opponents.
findings.metric: share of swindle wins (fell to <= 20%, then won) in which the other side lost on time
findings.n: n=151 player swindle wins, n=102 opponents
findings.caveat: In blitz swindles end more often by stalemate (0.13 vs 0.18) or repetition/agreed/insufficient (0.22 vs 0.25).

findings.claim: In rapid almost no swindle wins come by the other side flagging.
findings.metric: share of swindle wins (fell to <= 20%, then won) in which the other side lost on time
findings.n: n=45 player swindle wins, n=31 opponents
findings.caveat: Small samples; rapid swindles mostly end by repetition/agreed/insufficient (0.36 vs 0.41).

findings.claim: In bullet 69% of the player's swindles ended as wins rather than draws, against 63% of the opponents' swindles.
findings.metric: share of swindles (fell to <= 20%, did not lose) that ended as a win
findings.caveat: Descriptive share, no CI. Blitz 0.63 vs 0.55; rapid 0.59 vs 0.53.

findings.claim: The net expected points given away (opponents' ep lost minus the player's) correlates strongly with the player's score, so ep_loss measures what decides games.
findings.metric: Pearson correlation between net_ep per game and the player's score over all games
findings.caveat: Score by net_ep bin is monotone and steep: 0.064 [0.053, 0.076] in the -0.5 to -0.2 bin, 0.951 [0.940, 0.961] in the 0.2 to 0.5 bin.

findings.claim: From positions the pooled model rates 80-90% the player wins more often than the opponents do, and both more often than the model says: the model is under-confident at the extremes.
findings.metric: observed win rate of a side from positions after a move binned by that side's model P(win) 0.8-0.9; all time classes pooled
findings.caveat: Positions, not games, with CIs by game; the same fact as the conversion and swindle gaps in section 4.

findings.claim: From balanced positions the pooled model rates 40-50% the player wins more often than the opponents do.
findings.metric: observed win rate of a side from positions after a move binned by that side's model P(win) 0.4-0.5; all time classes pooled
findings.caveat: In every bin the player wins more often than opponents from positions the model rates the same; e.g. 0.1-0.2: 0.093 [0.081, 0.106] vs 0.056 [0.047, 0.065].
